description_verifiable_only: Patient age, released as 10 ordered bins from '< 12' to '>= 74' (years).
cost_rationale: Age is recorded at registration at no marginal cost and is a well-established CKD risk factor.

description_verifiable_only: Diastolic blood pressure indicator, released as a binary 0/1 flag.
cost_rationale: Blood pressure is measured with a reusable sphygmomanometer; the marginal cost per patient is effectively zero.
uncertainty_note: The column is named for diastolic pressure but ships as a binary 0/1 flag, so the underlying mmHg value and the threshold that produced the flag are both unrecoverable. The direction of the coding (1 = elevated) is inferred from its association with 'bp limit' and 'htn', not from documentation.

description_verifiable_only: Three-level blood-pressure indicator (0/1/2).
cost_rationale: Derived from the same sphygmomanometer reading as 'bp (Diastolic)', so it adds no marginal cost.
uncertainty_note: Undocumented. Empirically it refines 'bp (Diastolic)': every patient with bp (Diastolic)=0 has bp limit=0, while bp (Diastolic)=1 splits across all three levels. It is therefore most likely a graded severity band, but the mmHg cut-points are unknown and are NOT reconstructed here.

description_verifiable_only: Hypertension, binary 0/1.
cost_rationale: Elicited as history or read from an existing chart entry; no consumables required.

description_verifiable_only: Diabetes mellitus, binary 0/1.
cost_rationale: Treated as a history item: a previously established diagnosis is free to elicit at screening. Verified empirically NOT to be a deterministic function of the blood-glucose column, so it carries independent history information.
uncertainty_note: A first-time diabetes diagnosis requires a glucose assay, so in a population with poor prior healthcare contact this variable would be less freely available than assumed here.

description_verifiable_only: Coronary artery disease, binary 0/1.
cost_rationale: Recorded as a prior diagnosis during history taking; free to elicit at the point of screening.
uncertainty_note: Establishing CAD de novo is expensive. Its value as a *screening* predictor depends on patients already knowing the diagnosis.

description_verifiable_only: Appetite, binary 0/1.
cost_rationale: A single symptom question; no cost.
uncertainty_note: Polarity (whether 1 denotes poor or good appetite) is not documented in the released file.

description_verifiable_only: Pedal oedema, binary 0/1.
cost_rationale: Established by inspection and palpation of the ankles; no consumables.

description_verifiable_only: Anaemia, binary 0/1.
cost_rationale: Conservatively tiered as laboratory-derived. Anaemia is defined by a haemoglobin concentration, and in a dataset that also ships 'hemo' the most likely provenance of this flag is the full blood count.
uncertainty_note: IMPORTANT AND CONSEQUENTIAL. Anaemia can also be recorded clinically (conjunctival or palmar pallor) at no cost. We verified that 'ane' is NOT a deterministic function of the 'hemo' bins (for example 25 patients with hemo 10-11.3 are ane=0 while 3 are ane=1), so it is not a pure re-coding of haemoglobin. Because provenance cannot be established from the file, it is EXCLUDED from the low-cost configuration. This is the conservative choice: it can only understate low-cost performance, never inflate it.

description_verifiable_only: Urine specific gravity, 5 ordered bins from '< 1.007' to '>= 1.023'.
cost_rationale: Read directly from a urine reagent strip; non-invasive and among the cheapest measurements available in any clinic.

description_verifiable_only: Urine albumin, 5 ordered bins ('< 0' to '>= 4'), i.e. a dipstick protein/albumin grade.
cost_rationale: Read from the same urine reagent strip as 'sg'; non-invasive and cheap. Albuminuria is one of the two axes on which CKD is defined, which makes it both the most clinically relevant and the most scrutinised low-cost variable in this study.

description_verifiable_only: Urine sugar, 6 bins from '< 0' to '>= 4'.
cost_rationale: Read from the same urine reagent strip; non-invasive and cheap.
uncertainty_note: The published bin edges for this column are internally inconsistent and overlapping ('1 - 2' vs '2 - 2'; '3 - 4' vs '4 - 4' vs '>= 4'), so its ordinal encoding contains ties. Reported as a data-quality defect; not silently repaired.

description_verifiable_only: Red blood cells in urine, binary 0/1.
cost_rationale: Requires urine microscopy: non-invasive to the patient, but needs a microscope and a trained operator, so it is not free at the point of community screening.
uncertainty_note: Could in principle refer to a blood-count red-cell abnormality rather than urinary red cells, but its position among the urinalysis columns and the presence of a separate 'rbcc' (red blood cell count) column make urinary microscopy the far more likely reading.

description_verifiable_only: Pus cells in urine, binary 0/1.
cost_rationale: Urine microscopy; same infrastructure requirement as 'rbc'.

description_verifiable_only: Pus cell clumps in urine, binary 0/1.
cost_rationale: Urine microscopy; same infrastructure requirement as 'rbc'.

description_verifiable_only: Bacteria in urine, binary 0/1.
cost_rationale: Urine microscopy; same infrastructure requirement as 'rbc'.

description_verifiable_only: Blood glucose (random), 10 bins from '< 112' to '>= 448' mg/dL.
cost_rationale: Venous or capillary blood assay.

description_verifiable_only: Blood urea, 8 bins from '< 48.1' to '>= 352.9' mg/dL.
cost_rationale: Serum chemistry panel; requires venepuncture and an analyser.

description_verifiable_only: Serum creatinine, 7 bins from '< 3.65' to '>= 28.85' mg/dL.
cost_rationale: Serum chemistry panel; requires venepuncture and an analyser.
uncertainty_note: Serum creatinine is the input to the eGFR equation that defines 'grf' and 'stage'. It is retained in the valid laboratory configuration because it is a genuine, routinely measured screening analyte rather than a diagnostic label, but it is the variable most likely to behave as a near-proxy for the outcome, and results are interpreted with that in mind.

description_verifiable_only: Serum sodium, 9 bins from '< 118' to '>= 158' mEq/L.
cost_rationale: Serum electrolyte panel; requires venepuncture.

description_verifiable_only: Serum potassium, 4 bins from '< 7.31' to '>= 42.59' mEq/L.
cost_rationale: Serum electrolyte panel; requires venepuncture.
uncertainty_note: Near-constant: 197 of 200 patients fall in the single bin '< 7.31'. The upper bins ('38.18 - 42.59', '>= 42.59') lie far outside any survivable serum potassium range and are almost certainly recording errors. Flagged, retained as-is, and carries essentially no usable information.

description_verifiable_only: Haemoglobin, 10 bins from '< 6.1' to '>= 16.5' g/dL.
cost_rationale: Full blood count; requires venepuncture and an analyser.

description_verifiable_only: Packed cell volume (haematocrit), 10 bins from '< 17.9' to '>= 49.1' percent.
cost_rationale: Full blood count; requires venepuncture.

description_verifiable_only: Red blood cell count, 9 bins from '< 2.69' to '>= 7.41' (millions/uL).
cost_rationale: Full blood count; requires venepuncture.

description_verifiable_only: White blood cell count, 9 bins from '< 4980' to '>= 24020' (cells/uL).
cost_rationale: Full blood count; requires venepuncture.

description_verifiable_only: Glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), 10 bins plus one invalid entry.
cost_rationale: eGFR is computed from serum creatinine and is the quantity that *defines* CKD stage. Using it to predict CKD is close to using the diagnostic criterion itself as a predictor.

description_verifiable_only: CKD stage s1 to s5.
cost_rationale: A staging label assigned after diagnosis. Empirically it is a deterministic banding of 'grf' in this file, and stages s3 and s5 are 100 percent CKD, so it encodes the outcome almost directly.

description_verifiable_only: Binary 0/1 flag.
cost_rationale: An exact one-to-one copy of the outcome 'class' in all 200 rows (ckd maps to 1, notckd maps to 0). It is the target, renamed.

description_verifiable_only: Outcome: 'ckd' or 'notckd'.
cost_rationale: The prediction target.
